prompt: git status --short prints ?? images/. What does that mean?
hint: Two question marks: Git has no idea about it.

choices.text: The folder is untracked
choices.why: Right. commit -a leaves it out.

choices.text: The folder has a conflict
choices.why: Conflicts show as UU, lesson 6.

choices.text: The folder was deleted
choices.why: A deletion shows as D.

choices.text: The folder is ignored
choices.why: Ignored files are not listed at all.

prompt: Why did git commit -am leave the picture behind?
hint: -a stages changes to files Git already knows.

choices.text: Pictures are too large for Git
choices.why: This one is three bytes; Git would take it.

choices.text: -a only covers tracked files
choices.why: Right. A new file needs git add first.

choices.text: The images folder was in .gitignore
choices.why: Then status would not have listed it.

choices.text: -m replaces the staged files
choices.why: -m only gives the message.

prompt: Why does cloning the branch into /tmp/fresh reveal the problem?

choices.text: It runs the check with more permissions
choices.why: Permissions have nothing to do with it.

choices.text: It downloads a newer check-links.sh
choices.why: The script is the same one.

choices.text: It has only what was pushed
choices.why: Right. What everybody else will get.

choices.text: Git hides untracked files in /tmp
choices.why: The file simply never went up.

prompt: Which of these can make code work on one machine and not another? Choose all that apply.
hint: True on the author's machine and nowhere else.

choices.text: A file that was never added
choices.why: Yes. The most common one.

choices.text: A secret in a local environment variable
choices.why: Yes. The code depends on it silently.

choices.text: Menu.html linked as menu.html
choices.why: Yes. Case differs on Linux.

choices.text: A long commit message
choices.why: Messages do not change what runs.

prompt: When it works on my machine reaches the team, who usually pays for it?

choices.text: Only the author, who fixes it
choices.why: The fix is cheap; finding it was somebody else's time.

choices.text: Nobody; it is found eventually
choices.why: Being found costs whoever finds it.

choices.text: The hosting service
choices.why: It stores what it is given.

choices.text: Somebody else, later, for more
choices.why: Right. Bruno, Diego, or a customer.

prompt: What does CI do on each pull request?
hint: A machine that belongs to nobody.

choices.text: Merges it once it has an approval
choices.why: CI checks; merging is a separate decision.

choices.text: Reviews the code in place of a person
choices.why: It runs checks; it does not read for meaning.

choices.text: Runs the checks on a clean clone
choices.why: Right. And marks the pull request green or red.

choices.text: Deploys the branch to customers
choices.why: Checking comes before any release.

prompt: In the workflow, what does the step uses: actions/checkout@v5 give the run?

choices.text: A copy of Ana's laptop
choices.why: Nothing of anybody's laptop is on it.

choices.text: The branch exactly as pushed
choices.why: Right. Which is why the missing picture shows up.

choices.text: The latest version of main
choices.why: It is the pull request's branch.

choices.text: The previous run's files
choices.why: Each run starts on a fresh machine.

prompt: How does CI know check-links.sh failed?

choices.text: It reads the word missing in the output
choices.why: The text is for people; the exit status is for CI.

choices.text: It compares with the last run
choices.why: Each run is judged on its own.

choices.text: The exit status is not zero
choices.why: Right. exit $status ends with 1 when anything is missing.

choices.text: A person marks it failed
choices.why: It is automatic.

prompt: A check passes when its script ends with exit status ___.
How does a team stop a red cross from being ignored?

choices.text: It asks everybody to be careful
choices.why: That is the habit CI was replacing.

choices.text: It emails the author
choices.why: An email can be ignored too.

choices.text: It runs the checks twice
choices.why: Twice red is still ignorable.

choices.text: A protected main needs green checks
choices.why: Right. Nothing merges past a red one.

prompt: Which of these can CI not check?
hint: A script answers yes or no questions.

choices.text: Whether every link points to a file
choices.why: check-links.sh does exactly that.

choices.text: Whether the tests pass
choices.why: Running tests is CI's main job.

choices.text: Whether the text is clear to a customer
choices.why: Right. That needs a person.

choices.text: Whether the site builds
choices.why: Building is a script like any other.

prompt: Match each statement to what it belongs to.
hint: One applies to every ticket, one to one ticket.

pairs.left: The menu shows gluten, milk and eggs
Tested by Diego on a phone
Reviewed and approved by somebody else

prompt: Under the bakery's definition, when is #34 done?
hint: Read the list to the end.

choices.text: When the picture shows on Ana's laptop
choices.why: That is the bottom rung.

choices.text: When the pull request is merged
choices.why: Testing and release are still ahead.

choices.text: When Diego has tested it
choices.why: It still has to be released and looked at.

choices.text: When it is released and seen live
choices.why: Right. And its acceptance criteria are met.

prompt: How does a definition of done make estimates more honest?
hint: What does a 3 have to include?

choices.text: It fixes each point to a number of hours
choices.why: Points stay relative.

choices.text: A size then includes testing and release
choices.why: Right. Done includes them, so the size does.

choices.text: It removes the need to estimate
choices.why: It changes what is estimated.

choices.text: It makes every ticket the same size
choices.why: Tickets still differ.

prompt: A missing file can be caught at each of these points. Put them from cheapest to most expensive.
hint: The lower on the ladder, the cheaper.
items: A customer on the live site
trap: A customer finding it costs trust, which no command gives back.

prompt: Put the rungs of the ladder in order, from the bottom.
trap: Releasing before testing puts Diego's findings in front of customers.

prompt: Which of these are true? Choose all that apply.
hint: One is about git status, one about who decides.

choices.text: An empty git status means nothing is left behind
choices.why: Yes. Nothing modified, nothing untracked.

choices.text: Each developer decides what done means for them
choices.why: The team decides once, together.

choices.text: A ticket is done when both its criteria and the DoD are met
choices.why: Yes. Both.

choices.text: CI replaces testing by a person
choices.why: It covers what a script can see.
